key_insight: Instead of relying on repeated sampling of full answers, the paper learns a small semantic search policy that generates diverse concepts/hints to steer a larger LLM toward better reasoning solutions.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to spend test-time compute more efficiently by training a lightweight controller that improves a frozen model’s reasoning performance without retraining the large model itself.
method: Sample problem-specific concepts, hints, or strategies before answer generation rather than only adding decoding noise.
Use a multi-concept trajectory to encourage semantic diversity in the search space.
Train a small concept generator with reinforcement learning so its outputs maximize downstream success of a fixed large answer model.
evidence_signal: On hard mathematical reasoning tasks, the trained concept generator improved pass@k over naive repeated sampling at the same answer-generation budget and transferred to unseen answer models, including a different model family.
watch_item: The approach adds a learned intermediate generation step, so its gains may depend on careful reward design and robust concept quality across tasks and target models.
paper_title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
